summary:
As of July 2026 Vermont is listed among the most protective US states on gender-identity nondiscrimination, though a national legal risk assessment notes that the federal layer is under attack through the DC House bathroom ban, so that tier on its own can no longer be considered fully protective.

State law bans discrimination based on gender identity in employment, public accommodations, education, housing, credit, insurance and union practices. The provision was added after a 2006 veto, passed again in 2007, signed May 22, 2007 by Governor Jim Douglas, and took effect July 1, 2007. The anti-bullying law also prohibits bullying, cyberbullying and harassment based on gender identity in all educational institutions.

Hate crime law provides additional penalties for a crime committed based on the victim's gender identity, added in 1999 to the 1990 law that originally covered sexual orientation. The gay and/or trans panic defence was abolished by legislation passed 144-1 in the House in March 2021 and 29-0 in the Senate in April 2021, signed May 5, 2021 by Governor Phil Scott and effective July 1.

Use of conversion therapy on LGBT minors, which includes transgender minors, was banned by a bill approved unanimously in the Senate March 17, 2016, approved with amendments in the House April 26, accepted by the Senate April 29, signed May 25 by Governor Peter Shumlin and effective July 1, 2016. Vermont enacted S.132 (Act 138) signed May 25, 2016 prohibiting conversion therapy on minors and treating its performance on minors as unprofessional conduct under 18 V.S.A. §§ 8351-8353 and related 26 V.S.A. licensing statutes.

Vermont permits both preoperative and post-operative transgender individuals to change the gender marker on birth certificates and other state-issued documents upon court order supported by a letter from a licensed medical or mental health practitioner of surgical, hormonal, or other appropriate treatment for gender transition. Effective July 1, 2022, individuals born in Vermont can legally change sex marker to male, female or X based on self-determination without court order, mental health diagnosis, surgery, divorce or medical permission under a bill signed in April 2022 (H.628, Act 88, approved April 6, 2022, amending 18 V.S.A. § 5112 to allow issuance of a new birth certificate to reflect gender identity). Since July 1, 2019 the Department of Motor Vehicles has offered X on driver's licences and state IDs with no documentation needed.

Since July 1, 2018 all single-user public bathrooms must be marked as gender-neutral under a bill signed in May 2018. Since 2013 all health insurers underwriting in Vermont are required to cover transgender care including sex reassignment surgery. In May 2023 a law effective immediately by emergency clause legally protects, defends and shields transgender and non-binary people accessing gender-affirming healthcare across state lines coming into Vermont; Vermont has shield laws enacted in 2023 and 2024 that are enforceable against out-of-state action.

In October 2023 the Department of Education unanimously passed a policy to protect and defend transgender and non-binary students within schools and classrooms. In 2023 Mid Vermont Christian School's girls' basketball team forfeited a match against a team fielding a transgender girl citing fairness and safety and was as a result forbidden from competition by the Vermont Principals' Association.
tangentialFactors:
Vermont's protective posture sits inside a national environment where federal measures restrict passport markers, entry screening and care access, so state-level protection does not insulate a trans visitor from federal processing at borders and airports.

The state's shield laws, enforceable against out-of-state action, are designed to resist interstate legal reach, but their practical effect against federal action is not documented in these sources.

Vermont's history of legislative action on LGBT rights stretches back decades, including civil unions from July 2000 and same-sex marriage since September 1, 2009, the first state to adopt it via legislature and governor rather than court decision, indicating sustained political support rather than a recent or fragile settlement.
localsOnly:
Residents can change their birth certificate sex marker to male, female or X by self-determination without court order, diagnosis, surgery or medical permission since July 1, 2022 under Act 88. Driver's licences and state IDs have offered an X marker with no documentation since July 1, 2019.

State employees' same-sex partners have received benefits since 1994. Vermont law permits single LGBT individuals and same-sex couples to petition to adopt, provides lesbian couples access to in vitro fertilization with recognition of the non-genetic, non-gestational mother as legal parent to a child born via donor insemination irrespective of marital status, and in June 1993 the Vermont Supreme Court ruled in favor of a lesbian seeking to adopt her partner's two biological sons.

Discrimination based on sexual orientation in employment, public accommodations, education, housing, credit, insurance and union practices was banned with protections added in 1992, and hate crime legislation enacted in 1990 including sexual orientation provides additional penalties.

Historic statutes criminalising sodomy and oral sex were enacted, reduced and repealed between 1861 and April 1977; adult private consensual noncommercial sodomy is unenforceable under Lawrence v. Texas.
outOfScopeNotes:
The sources do not document how Vermont's shield laws would operate against federal action, or whether any Vermont-specific enforcement incidents involving trans people have occurred; this remains unresolved.

Whether Vermont has any state-level analogue to the federal passport or entry-screening restrictions, or any pending legislation rolling back the protections listed, is not sourced here and should be verified against current legislative records before travel.

The claim that Vermont is among the most protective states rests on a single July 2026 assessment; comparative rankings against other states are not independently sourced in this inventory.
